pilot.summary: Game four of four at Alex's house in Orinda, three-player with Alex and Stuart, and the one win of the night. I ramped through the early removal and the table spent its wipes on my mid-tier dinosaurs, which let me rebuild faster than they could answer — and meant that with my own board empty, Blasphemous Act cleared theirs at no cost to me. Then Gishath swung at Stuart for 7 and revealed five dinosaurs off the trigger, one of which made their creatures enter tapped. Next turn Enlarge made it a 14-point swing into 7 already dealt, lethal by commander damage, with two more dinosaurs off the second trigger. No changes to the deck.

read.what_it_does: One game is logged, so this is what that evening showed rather than a pattern. In game 001 the deck ramped through the early removal and kept putting mid-tier dinosaurs back faster than the table could wipe them, and those bodies were not what won — they soaked the removal until Gishath could land. The win came off two commander triggers: a swing at Stuart for 7 revealing five dinosaurs, one of which made their creatures enter tapped, then Enlarge for +7/+7 the next turn, 14 into the 7 already dealt for lethal commander damage, revealing two more dinosaurs (001).
read.how_it_plays: From the one game logged: it looked ordinary enough for long enough that the table aimed its wipes at the mid-tier board, then turned lethal in two swings once the commander connected (001). Having my own board already cleared is what made Blasphemous Act one-sided — the sequencing did that, not the card (001). That was a three-player pod and it is the deck's whole record, so there is nothing here about how it sits in a bigger pod, or how it plays from behind.
mindful_of: In the one game logged (001), the table spent its wraths on the mid-tier dinosaurs and had nothing left when Gishath arrived. That was my read of one evening — it is not yet a pattern, and a table that has seen this deck once may not misread it twice.
Blasphemous Act was free for me only because my own board had already been answered (001). It is not automatically one-sided.

The record is one game and it is a win, so there is no logged evidence about what happens when Gishath is answered, when the ramp does not come, or in a four- or five-player pod. Nothing has tested that yet.
read.what_changed: Nothing has moved. The list has been on V3 since 2026-07-28 and game 001 was played on it; I made no changes after the win and wrote that the deck was working as designed (001). There is no version-to-version comparison to make until a second game is logged.
